title: Build the line, then use it
subtitle: Linear equations in two variables · 8 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **8 of the official questions in Linear equations in two variables are this one** — 0 Easy, 2 Medium, 6 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You're given a y-intercept plus another point (or a table), sometimes with a shift up or down, and asked for a missing coordinate of a third point, or the x-intercept of the new line.
- The question has more than one step and is usually hard.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Find the slope from the two known points and write y = mx + b.
- 2) Apply any shift to b (shifting down by k units changes b to b - k).
- 3) Substitute the known coordinate of the target point, or set y = 0 for the x-intercept, and solve.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Enter y = mx + b with m and b as sliders, adjust until the line passes through the given points, then trace to the target x-value or to the x-intercept.
For a shift, type the second line as y = (first line) - k.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You shift the x-intercept by the translation amount instead of shifting b, you solve for the original line's intercept and forget the shift, or you mix up which coordinate of the target point is unknown.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.

You shift the x-intercept by the translation amount instead of shifting b, you solve for the original line's intercept and forget the shift, or you mix up which coordinate of the target point is unknown.
